note: Adapted from Chhotani's (1997) species description; the original is in English. The soldier description follows Silvestri's (1922) original description and figures, no specimens having been seen; the alate is recorded as unknown; distribution records, synonymic citations, figure numbers and taxonomic discussion are not included.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Soldier body length 4.60 mm, head capsule nearly rectangular and about 1.5 times as long as wide, anterior lateral tubercles short and conical, the labral apex with a long horn-like point, the left mandible strongly twisted and as long as the head; worker head wider than long, antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 about 1/3 shorter than segment 2.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head rusty yellowish brown; mandibles nearly black; body creamy white. Head rather hairy, body densely covered with long and short hairs. Body length 4.60 mm. Head capsule nearly rectangular, about 1.5 times as long as wide, length without mandibles 1.84 mm, width 1.20 mm; sides slightly convergent anteriorly; frons gradually inclined forwards; anterior lateral tubercles short, conical; coronal suture only partly distinct. Fontanelle small, situated on the anterior part of the frontal slope. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 as long as segment 2 and slightly longer than segment 4. Labrum asymmetrical, apex with a long horn-like point; median length equal to width; anterolateral margins with small serrations. Mandibles asymmetrical; left mandible strongly twisted, as long as the head, length 1.84 mm; right mandible blade-like, with a long apical blade. Pronotum narrower than the head, anterior lobe weakly concave. Dorsal spur of the fore tibia short.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head pale ochre; body creamy white. Head rather hairy, with long and short hairs. Body length 4.00 mm. Head wider than long, length 0.90 mm, width 1.10 mm. Antennae 14-segmented, segment 3 about 1/3 shorter than segment 2 and slightly longer than segment 4. Postclypeus distinctly convex, about half as long as wide. Anterior lobe of the pronotum with almost no incision. Outer spur of the fore tibia very small, almost as in the soldier.
